$comment: Ranked toolchain applied by scripts/bootstrap.ts (public/bootstrap.mjs). Schema: Tool in lib/catalog/schema.ts. Secrets come from ~/.config/design-infra/secrets.env, never this file.

tools.name: design-infra (this repo)
tools.why: The router: ranked catalog, design systems, playbooks, taste memory and the @oc registry. Every other tool is chosen through it.
tools.use: Always. plan_ui for pages, propose_options for one component, search_components for pieces.

setup.command: claude plugin marketplace add OwenCoonahan/design-infra --scope project && claude plugin install design-infra@oc-design --scope project
setup.note: optional — adds the skills/hooks for teammates; restart the agent and verify tool availability

setup.text: UI work goes through design-infra: plan_ui (new pages from a brief), propose_options (one component: animate/restyle/add a state — show options WITH links, let the user pick), search_components (specific pieces). For new pages inspect plan_ui research.sources before composing: product screens/flows for apps and data, Landbook/Minimal Gallery for websites, Component Gallery for anatomy. For a section inspect its references. Research even when no gallery is named; map observations to reusable components. Show options unless choosing and building is already authorized, then implement and report sources afterward. Mobbin is optional and requires the user's supported account and OAuth; continue with accessible sources when unavailable. Never hand-build what the catalog has.
Follow ./DESIGN.md (moods, motion language, tokens). Theme tokens only — no hard-coded colours.

tools.name: shadcn/ui CLI + MCP + skill
tools.why: Every registry (ours, Aceternity, Magic UI, Kibo, Cult UI, React Bits…) installs through it; its MCP browses them all.
tools.use: Installing any component; plain app primitives (dialog, select, table, sidebar, chart) come from stock shadcn first.

setup.command: DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 npx -y skills@latest add shadcn/ui --skill shadcn -a claude-code codex -y

tools.name: Motion + @oc/motion-presets
tools.why: The animation engine under ~500 catalog entries; presets keep hand-written motion on the project's motion language.
tools.use: Any animation not covered by a drop-in component: layoutId indicators, exits, whileInView, scroll-linked, springs.

setup.text: Animations: use motion/react with lib/motion-presets.ts (motionPreset()) and the theme's tokens (duration-(--motion-fast) ease-motion-out). Wrap the app in <MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">. No Motion+ APIs (Ticker, Cursor, AnimateNumber, splitText…) without a licence.

tools.name: Motion AI Kit (skill + docs MCP)
tools.why: Motion's own free skill (best practices, perf, a11y) + docs search MCP. design-infra decides WHAT; this knows HOW.
tools.use: Whenever an agent writes Motion code.

setup.command: DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 npx -y skills@latest add motiondivision/ai-kit --skill motion -a claude-code codex -y

tools.name: Magic UI
tools.why: Polished, mostly token-friendly animated components (marquee, blur-fade, number-ticker, border-beam); MIT; best free source of tasteful motion.
tools.use: Landing-page polish, text/number animation, subtle wrappers.

setup.command: DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 npx -y skills@latest add magicuidesign/magicui -a claude-code codex -y

tools.name: SmoothUI
tools.why: ~230 MIT motion components + blocks on shadcn tokens with the best free AI/agent set (approval, tool call, task list, reasoning) and reduced-motion handling in most items.
tools.use: AI/agent surfaces; tabs, scroll-aware navbar, skeletons, carousels and reading progress. Set --brand: var(--primary) once (its tokens.json defaults to pink).

setup.text: SmoothUI: npx shadcn@latest add @smoothui/<name> installs to components/smoothui/<name>/index.tsx. Many items pull its tokens.json (bg-brand, smooth-N greys) — keep `--brand: var(--primary);` in :root of globals.css so they follow the theme.

tools.name: Motion Primitives
tools.why: Unstyled Motion wrappers (in-view, text-effect, transition-panel, animated-background) — safest way to add motion to YOUR components.
tools.use: 'Animate this' on existing components; tabs/panels/lists/headlines.

tools.name: transitions.dev (skill + MCP)
tools.why: Tuned CSS micro-interaction recipes applied to your markup (modal, tabs, toast, number pop, success check); free tier is plenty.
tools.use: Polish passes: press/hover, open/close timing, state feedback — zero dependencies.

setup.command: DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 npx -y skills@latest add Jakubantalik/transitions.dev --skill transitions-dev transitions-polish -a claude-code codex -y

tools.name: Origin UI (coss origin)
tools.why: ~600 theme-aware app components (inputs, tables, calendars, navbars) — the best free source for product UI that just follows the theme.
tools.use: App UI variants beyond stock shadcn: fields, filters, data tables, date pickers, command menus.

setup.text: Origin UI comps install by URL: npx shadcn@latest add https://coss.com/origin/r/comp-<N>.json — they also install Origin's own ui/* primitives; review overwrite prompts.

tools.name: Aceternity UI (free)
tools.why: The most-used flashy marketing components (spotlights, beams, scroll effects) — but hard-coded colours and 174 Pro-only blocks.
tools.use: Hero/background/scroll moments on marketing pages; convert colours to tokens after install. Free components only.

tools.name: Agentation (visual feedback)
tools.why: Click any element in the running app, annotate it, and the agent gets selector + source file — the fastest 'fix THIS' loop.
tools.use: Design review of a running UI; pairs with the refine skill.

setup.command: DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 npx -y skills@latest add benjitaylor/agentation --skill agentation -a claude-code codex -y

setup.text: Agentation: mount <Agentation endpoint="http://localhost:4747" /> in the root layout only when NODE_ENV === 'development'. Check pending annotations via the agentation MCP when the user says 'check my feedback'.

tools.name: Kage (design reference MCP)
tools.why: Free, keyless MCP over 372 analysed real product designs and 1,978 extracted components with prompts — how real products solved a section, beyond our catalog.
tools.use: Researching a page or section ('fintech pricing pages', 'a site like Linear for X') before planning; never for bulk export.

setup.text: For design references beyond the catalog — e.g. 'how do fintech pricing pages look' — use the kage MCP (search_designs, design_brief); never bulk-download.

tools.verify: curl -sf -X POST https://kage.design/mcp -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"verify","version":"0"}}}' >/dev/null

tools.name: Kibo UI
tools.why: Complex theme-aware product components (kanban, gantt, editor, dropzone, color picker) you'd never hand-build.
tools.use: Rich app features; its hosted MCP is currently broken (HTTP 500) — use the shadcn MCP instead.

tools.name: Cult UI
tools.why: Playful, tactile components and onboarding flows; theming varies by generation.
tools.use: Consumer/playful projects (lively motion); check colours after install.

tools.name: React Bits
tools.why: The deepest well of creative text effects, WebGL backgrounds and micro-interactions — heavy deps, purple defaults, Commons Clause (install-only).
tools.use: Cinematic/experimental pages. Names are case-sensitive: @react-bits/SplitText-TS-TW.

tools.name: Beautiful UI
tools.why: The best free AI/agent surfaces (thinking traces, approvals, tool chips) — its foundation.css redefines --accent.
tools.use: AI products; import foundation.css BEFORE your theme or rename its accent vars.

tools.name: libraries.dev packages
tools.why: Small MIT npm packages for AI interfaces: thinking-orbs, border-beam, voice-glow, bot-avatars, metal-fx.
tools.use: Install per need (e.g. pnpm add thinking-orbs) — @oc/agent-status and @oc/beam-card wrap two of them.

tools.name: 21st.dev (CLI + MCP)

secrets.note: free account; component code is metered

tools.why: Breadth: 12k+ community components and search when nothing curated fits. Quality varies.
tools.use: Searching for something specific the catalog lacks; read the code before shipping.

setup.name: 21st
setup.command: claude mcp add -s user --transport http 21st https://21st.dev/api/mcp -H "x-api-key: ${API_KEY_21ST}"

tools.name: Kitbitz (CC0 illustrations MCP)
tools.why: 2,043 hand-drawn CC0 illustrations in 13 consistent kits, searchable through a free read-only MCP — warmth for empty states and onboarding without an illustrator.
tools.use: Empty states, onboarding, 404s and marketing spots on warm/playful products; download the chosen SVGs into the project.

setup.text: Illustrations: search the kitbitz MCP (search_illustrations, then get_illustration) and download the chosen SVGs into public/illustrations/ — CC0, no attribution; stay within one kit per product and don't hotlink assets.kitbitz.art.

tools.verify: curl -sf -X POST https://mcp.kitbitz.art -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"verify","version":"0"}}}' >/dev/null

tools.name: OriginKit (CLI + MCP)

secrets.note: Profile → API Keys; free = 10 copies/day, Pro $79/yr

tools.why: ~1,100 WebGL/shader backgrounds, heroes and cursors — the wow factor, metered and proprietary.
tools.use: A signature background/hero when the free catalog looks too familiar.

setup.name: originkit
setup.command: claude mcp add -s user --transport http originkit https://mcp.originkit.dev/mcp -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ORIGINKIT_API_KEY}"

setup.text: OriginKit: install with npx originkit add <slug> --auth $ORIGINKIT_API_KEY. NEVER run `originkit init` — it overwrites shadcn's components.json.

tools.name: Motion+ (premium components + MCP)

secrets.note: set MOTION_PLUS=1 once you have a membership; the MCP signs in via OAuth in /mcp

tools.why: Carousel, Ticker, AnimateNumber, Typewriter, Cursor, page transitions and all 460+ example sources.
tools.use: Only with a licence; then prefer it over hand-rolled versions of those components.

setup.text: Motion+ licensed: Motion+ components (motion-plus/react) and example sources are allowed; install from the Motion+ private registry (https://motion.dev/docs/react-motion-plus-installation).

tools.name: transitions.dev Pro
tools.why: React/TS variants of every recipe plus Pro transitions.
tools.use: When CSS recipes need to become typed React components.

setup.name: transitions-pro
setup.command: claude mcp add -s user --transport http transitions-pro https://api.transitions.dev/v1/agent/mcp -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TRANSITIONS_LICENSE}"

tools.name: Anatomy (isometric explainer skill)
tools.why: Specialist illustration tool for interactive explanations of mechanisms and technical concepts; the catalog supplies reusable anatomy-figures components first.
tools.use: Docs, educational articles and technical feature sections that need an explanatory SVG or WebGL figure. Select explicitly; ordinary controls use component libraries.

setup.command: DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 npx -y skills@latest add wheresryan22/anatomy --skill anatomy -a claude-code codex -y

setup.text: Anatomy: search existing anatomy/* figures before creating a custom explainer. Selected components use pnpm add anatomy-figures and a per-figure ESM import; map --anatomy-* to project tokens. The optional /anatomy skill creates new mechanisms; preserve factual accuracy, keyboard input, reduced motion and offscreen cleanup, then inspect the result on target devices.
